title: Trump Claims Iran Nuclear Deal Imminent After Strikes
description_short: Trump Claims Iran Nuclear Deal Imminent After Strikes
description_medium: Days after US and Israeli forces struck Iranian nuclear facilities, Trump publicly claimed a comprehensive nuclear deal with Iran was 'very close' and could be signed 'within days.' Iranian officials publicly contradicted Trump's characterization, with the foreign ministry calling the strikes a war crime. Trump's optimistic framing appeared at odds with the military and diplomatic realities on the ground. Critics questioned whether Trump was attempting to spin a military escalation as a diplomatic success.

title: EPA Rolls Back Clean Power Plan
description_short: EPA Rolls Back Clean Power Plan
description_medium: On October 10, 2017, EPA Administrator Scott Pruitt announced a proposal to repeal the Obama-era Clean Power Plan, which set carbon-pollution guidelines for existing power plants. Pruitt argued that the rule exceeded the agency's authority and said “the war on coal is over.” The announcement began a rulemaking process; it did not itself complete the repeal.
description_long: On October 10, 2017, EPA Administrator Scott Pruitt announced that the Trump administration would propose repealing the Clean Power Plan, an Obama-era regulation setting carbon-pollution guidelines for existing power plants. The EPA's October 16 Federal Register notice formally proposed repeal and stated the agency's legal position that the rule exceeded its statutory authority. The proposal changed the direction of federal climate regulation, but it was a step in rulemaking rather than an immediate removal of the existing requirements. Pruitt publicly framed the announcement as ending the “war on coal.” The Clean Power Plan had been designed to limit power-sector carbon emissions, so a repeal proposal created uncertainty for states, utilities, and communities planning around federal emissions rules. The supplied source documents the agency's proposal and legal rationale; it does not quantify any emissions change, prove that the action favored a specific company, or describe the final legal and regulatory outcome. The preserved title says “Rolls Back,” and the original medium calls the action a completed repeal that removed mandates. Those formulations go beyond the October 2017 source and require later records to establish what ultimately took effect.

preserved_fields.title: EPA Rolls Back Clean Power Plan
preserved_fields.description_short: EPA Rolls Back Clean Power Plan

notes: Rewrote the populated medium because it described a proposed repeal as a completed repeal and attributed unsupported effects. The linked Federal Register notice supports a proposed repeal and EPA's legal rationale, not the final outcome. The title still implies a completed rollback.
proposed_correction: Change the title to say EPA proposed repealing the Clean Power Plan, or add later rulemaking and court records establishing the final outcome.

title: “I Love the Poorly Educated” Rally Remark
description_short: “I Love the Poorly Educated” Rally Remark
description_medium: After winning the Nevada Republican caucus in February 2016, Donald Trump told supporters, “I love the poorly educated.” The crowd cheered, and the line became one of the most repeated remarks from his campaign. It was later cited as a symbol of his populist appeal and his embrace of anti-intellectual politics.

preserved_fields.description_short: “I Love the Poorly Educated” Rally Remark

notes: The ABC video is event-specific, but the packet supplies only the quotation and that it followed Trump's Nevada caucus win. proposed_correction: Add a neutral category for public conduct or campaign gaffes. Keep this entry to a concise account unless a transcript or further event context is supplied.

title: Over 10 Million Face Health Insurance Loss Under New Law
description_short: Over 10 Million Face Health Insurance Loss Under New Law
description_medium: By late July 2025, non-partisan projections indicated that over 10 million Americans would lose their health insurance as a direct result of the 'Big Beautiful Bill'. The sweeping cuts to Medicaid disproportionately affected low-income families and individuals with pre-existing conditions. Public health officials warned of an impending national health crisis with increased mortality rates.

title: Trump Fires 17 Inspectors General Overnight Without Congressional Notice
description_short: Trump Fires 17 Inspectors General Overnight Without Congressional Notice
description_medium: The supplied account says that hours after his January 20, 2025 inauguration, President Donald Trump dismissed 17 inspectors general without the 30-day notice to Congress required by law. The firings affected watchdog offices across agencies including Defense, State, and Transportation. The account says courts later found the removals unlawful, but gives no case or ruling details.
